Resolves the run_id collision trap flagged during RE17's design review: every run-scoped filesystem/ArtifactStore path in campaign_execution.py/campaign_workers.py is keyed on run_id alone, so run_campaign() derives a distinct execution run_id per lane from the shared campaign run_id plus the lane's own stable identity, rather than sharing one run_id across lanes -- fixed at this seam with no changes needed to the lower layers. Deliberately sequential, not a unified CampaignGraph across lanes. 10 new unit tests. Verified on real Brutus hardware: a two-lane run_campaign() call (stock + tune) sharing one campaign run_id succeeded on gfx1100 with distinct per-lane execution run_ids and no path collision, stock correctly skipping generate/workload/smoke and tune correctly running the full chain with build reuse.

technical-summary: HI68 (RV49/F2, P0): the noise-canary retry no longer replaces final-stage statistics. technical-summary: Fixed a real, intermittent flaky-test failure in tools/tests/test_pin_status.py::RemoteAndAggregateTests (test_complete_pass / test_aggregate_converged, different one failing on different loaded full-suite runs, each passing reliably in isolation) with GPT's diagnosis (gpt-auto-agent, request req_37641bb91ff4442c) confirming my own root-cause theory: the fixture creates two INDEPENDENT git repositories (fake tree 'a' in setUp(), fake tree 'b' inside each test method) whose root 'init' commits must hash identically for these tests to pass, since build_report()'s want = expected.get(...) or local.bigcherry_head falls back to comparing tree 'a's HEAD against tree 'b's HEAD verbatim when expected_tooling_revision="". Git commit hashes are sensitive to author/committer timestamp at 1-second resolution; _git()'s subprocess calls never pinned GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE, so the two independently-created commits (identical tree content, no parent, same committer identity) only hashed identically when both `git commit` calls landed in the same wall-clock second -- true most of the time in isolation, but crossed under a loaded full-suite run (a background HIP campaign build was running concurrently when this was first observed), producing genuinely different hashes for what the test fixture intended to be equivalent tooling revisions. GPT ruled out other candidates (tempdir path/casing, core.autocrlf, global signing config) as implausible given the specific 'sometimes matches, sometimes not' symptom, and explicitly recommended against weakening the test to compare tree hashes instead of commit identity, since the production check deliberately distinguishes commit identity (reviewed/released tooling revision) from mere source-tree equivalence. Applied the fix exactly as given: pin GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL/DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL/DATE (author/committer identity was already pinned via -c user.email/user.name; only the dates were missing) plus commit.gpgSign=false in _git()'s subprocess env, scoped entirely to this test file. Verified deterministic across 5 consecutive isolated runs and 2 consecutive full-suite runs (1460 passed, 3 skipped, 61 subtests both times, 0 flakes) -- previously this same full-suite run flaked on 1-2 tests in this class on 2 separate prior attempts this session.

technical-summary: HI64: fixed a real cross-device tuning-poison leak found via real dual-XTX hardware fault-injection testing, root-caused and fix-designed with GPT (req_c6a1d50e4f8b4d20, req_a83f4d26c42e492a) after multiple rounds of source-level verification against real line numbers. Fix: ggml_hip_tuner_resolve()'s public contract now returns a struct exposing measurement_failure explicitly (via a thin wrapper around a renamed internal impl, avoiding touching ~25 scattered exit sites); record_result() only lets a non-failed result replace a failed one for the same portable key, never the reverse; the impl's cache-hit check excludes failed entries; dispatch.cu gates the process-global g_bindings.emplace() (not the correctly-unconditional per-device/thread g_thread_bindings.insert()) on a new process_binding_cacheable flag, false for both a tuner failure and a related pre-existing capture-skip leak fixed in the same change. Verified: 9 new source-contract tests, full offline suite (1555 tests) passes; real compiler build on Brutus with zero errors; re-ran the exact fault-injection test that exposed the bug on real dual-XTX hardware, both device orders -- canonical measurements.jsonl now shows all 12 shapes clean (matching the no-injection baseline) while the crash-safe journal correctly preserves both the historical failure evidence and the eventual real success, exactly the intended state machine. This is the first hardware-validated confirmation of HI64's per-device poison scoping, not merely structurally sound.

technical-summary: GPT follow-up review of the HI64 cross-device poison-leak fix (2c32c7d) found two remaining issues, both verified against real source and fixed. (1) Concurrency race: the single-flight lock was acquired inside ggml_hip_tuner_resolve_impl() and released before the new wrapper ggml_hip_tuner_resolve()'s post-call g_results re-check, leaving a window where a second thread's failure->success replacement could land in between and cause the wrapper to report a stale measurement_failure for an invocation that actually failed. Fixed by moving g_single_flight_mutex acquisition into the wrapper, held across both the impl call and the re-check. (2) Incomplete capture-skip fix: dispatch.cu unconditionally cached native into g_thread_bindings on a capture-time skip, which would permanently starve that (thread,device,signature) triple even after capture ended, since capture -- unlike a fatal measurement failure -- is not a permanent condition. Fixed by adding a separate thread_binding_cacheable flag (false only for the capture-skip case) alongside the existing process_binding_cacheable flag, so g_thread_bindings.insert() is now also gated appropriately while a real measurement failure still unconditionally populates the thread-local cache (still useful locally). Verified: 4 new/updated tests in test_dispatch_safety.py, full offline suite 1546 passed / 3 skipped, real hardware re-validation on Brutus's dual gfx1100 pair via the fault-injection test that originally exposed the poison-leak bug -- canonical measurements.jsonl all clean (12/12), journal correctly preserving 12 failure rows + 12 success rows.

technical-summary: Second-round GPT review fix for the HI18 native SPLIT_REDUCE correctness probe. Real gfx1100 measurement, non-blocking, full test-backend-ops MUL_MAT sweep (1216/1216 tests passed): 1088 cold-path resolutions, 11,570 candidates, F_tune=0.5379% -- clears the close threshold, reproduced on a follow-up sweep (0.5182%). Closed as measured-not-worth-it; bit-exact reduction semantics left explicitly N/A since the implementation gate never opened. Kept the timing instrumentation as a permanent diagnostic (GGML_HIP_TUNE_CORRECTNESS_TIMING, matching HI87's precedent) including D2H bytes moved, with a documented reopen condition (F_tune>=2% reassess, >=5% prototype). Post-implementation review (same gpt session) returned PASS, verifying RAII scope placement, the compare_outputs refactor's semantic equivalence, and single-flight thread-safety by reading the actual mutex acquisition, not just trusting the comment; one P2 hardening fix applied (zero-cost-when-disabled). 10 new source-contract tests. Full offline suite: 1830 passed.
